description: The agent must: (1) Use the `openclaw config set` command with the exact deeply-nested key path `skills.entries.openclaw-backup-restore.env.OPENCLAW_BACKUP_REPO` to register the local bare repo path in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. (2) Locate and execute the `backup.sh` script specifically inside `~/.openclaw/skills/openclaw-backup-restore/scripts/` (not write their own rsync logic). (3) The script will: read the repo URL from openclaw.json, initialize `~/openclaw-backup/` as a git repo, copy the skill's `.gitignore` to `~/openclaw-backup/`, rsync `~/.openclaw/` respecting the gitignore exclusions (node_modules/, logs/, tmp/, dist/, completions/), generate a categorized commit summary using the bespoke path-label mapping (workspace/config/runtime/memory), commit with the format `chore: backup <categories>`, and push to the remote `main` branch. The proprietary trap: an agent relying on generic knowledge would write their own rsync/git commands, producing a commit message in an arbitrary format, missing the categorized labels, and failing to copy the .gitignore from the skill directory. The eval verifies the exact commit message format, absence of excluded directories, presence of .gitignore, and that the push reached the bare remote.
